description: MMA at Penn is a student-run organization at the University of Pennsylvania that provides students with safe, structured, and accessible opportunities to train in mixed martial arts through qualified coaching, appropriate equipment, dedicated training space, and protective flooring and mats. The organization also seeks to support student participation in sanctioned competitions by helping cover registration fees, travel-related expenses, and other costs necessary for competitive development.

name: Mock Trial at Penn
description: Mock Trial is a student group at the University of Pennsylvania - and the school's one and only competitive mock trial program! Since 1996, the Mock Trial team has traveled around the country to compete in some of the most prestigious tournaments—providing outlets for future lawyers, actors, debaters, and public speakers to refine their craft. Mock Trial refers to the act of simulating a trial. It’s a mix of public speaking, acting and debating. name: Model Congress at Penn
description: Model Congress at Penn, founded in 1997, is an entirely student-run organization open to all undergraduates of the University of Pennsylvania. Each spring, Model Congress at Penn hosts an elite four-day conference for high school students from around the country to debate bills written by their peers covering a variety of contemporary political issues. Additionally, the club sponsors panels, guest speakers, and various other events in order to discuss and enhance our understanding of the United States government, particularly the Congress and legislative process.

name: Models@Penn
description: Models@Penn is a student organization at the University of Pennsylvania dedicated to empowering students to embrace their individuality and build confidence through runway modeling. We strive to create a diverse and inclusive community that nurtures creativity, collaboration, and personal growth while helping members refine their runway skills and stage presence. description: Moso Capital (“Moso”) an undergraduate student club on Penn's campus part of Wharton Council. We provide students real-world investing experience by working directly with venture capitalists and angel investors to source, diligence, and recommend startups for investment. Our vision is to build the next generation of investors. We envision a community where students and investors partner and collaborate side-by-side, combining classroom theory with tangible, outcome-driven work that results in real investments.

name: Movimiento Estudiantil Chicano de Aztlan (MEChA de Penn)
description: El Movimiento Estudiantil Chicana/o de Aztlán (MEChA is an organization that supports the exploration of Chicano culture, works to recruit Chicano students to Penn, and also works with the Penn community to build dialogue across campus and build a social consciousness within the Latino community. MEChA is a student organization at Penn whose primary activities revolve around cultural exploration, not only around Chicano/Mexican-American culture, but Latina/o culture, Meso-American culture, history, and dialogue on issues varying from race, ethnicity, gender, religion, sexuality, and many other

description: Music Business at Penn is the premier music business student organization at the University of Pennsylvania. We continually strive to give our members an exclusive educational experience through weekly meetings, immersive speaker events, concerts, peer-to-peer mentorship, internship recruitment events, and more.​ The Penn community believes in change starting at the root of powerful ideas. description: MLSA welcomes the participation of all members of the Penn Law community and encourages the presence of Muslims from diverse schools of thought, levels of faith and backgrounds. MLSA hopes to foster a welcoming atmosphere for every law student wishing to learn more about Islam and/or gain support from their community.

name: Muslim Students' Association
description: We are a student group at the University of Pennsylvania. The Muslim Students Association is for students interested in the experience of Islam. We encourage and facilitate the personal, social, and spiritual development of Muslim students at Penn (undergraduate and graduate). Any student is welcome to join. We are open to all.

description: NAACP Chapter at the University of Pennsylvania Mission Statement: The University of Pennsylvania Chapter of the National Association for the Advancement of Colored People strives to ensure the social, political, economic, and educational equality of all persons here in the university community as well as the Greater West Philadelphia area through implementation of grassroots efforts such as direct action and community engagement.

Plus, we always provide free food at our events!

The organization seeks to engage both Nepali and non-Nepali students through cultural, social, and educational events, while also promoting outreach and collaboration with Nepali organizations locally and globally.

description: The Netter Center brings together the resources and assets of both the University and the wider community to help solve universal problems such as poverty, health inequities, environmental sustainability, and inadequate, and unequal education. The Netter Center Student Advisory Board was formed in 2001 to increase student involvement in the operation and strategic planning of the Netter Center. description: If you are curious about how the brain functions and how you can pursue a career in neuroscience or any related field, Neuroscience Society, a student organization at the University of Pennsylvania, is the perfect place for you! Join us for discussions, lectures, and workshops given by some of the world’s most prominent neurologists and neurosurgeons from the University. Membership is open to everyone—you don’t have to be Nigerian to get involved! Whether you identify with Nigeria directly, have roots elsewhere in Africa, or are simply curious to learn more about Nigerian culture, you’ll find a place here. NAP brings people together to celebrate culture, build friendships, and foster growth through speakers, social events, networking opportunities, community outreach, and scholarship.

description: NAPP is a student-led organization through the School of Nursing dedicated to applying nutrition science to clinical practice , preventive health , and everyday well-being . NAPP fosters interdisciplinary learning, hands-on experiences, and peer connection, helping nursing and pre-health students translate classroom knowledge into real-world health advocacy . Through workshops, community engagement (volunteering), and a focus on accessible nutrition, NAPP promotes whole-person care and advances health equity.

Founded on three pillars—education, service, and community—NEST provides opportunities for students to learn, give back, and build meaningful connections. description: Off The Beat is the premier modern rock & pop student a cappella group at the prestigious University of Pennsylvania. Rooted in rock music, our repertoire now spans a range of genres from pop and R&B to electronic and funk. Founded in 1987 and now in our 39th year, Off The Beat has become one of the most decorated collegiate a cappella groups in the US winning over 30 CARA Awards, being featured on 17 Best of Collegiate A Cappella (BOCA) albums, and starring in the second season of POP TV's aca-documentary television series, "Sing it On!"

We firmly believe that cultural exchange is crucial for building bridges of understanding between Omanis and the Penn community. Onda Latina has become an immensely popular name on this campus and in the Philadelphia community performing to sold-out crowds every semester. name: Outdoors Club at Penn
description: This student group brings together people who love the outdoors. We facilitate meeting like minded people, and planning and going on trips. We've got rock climbers, tree-huggers, hikers, bikers, and everything in between. The Outdoors Club is open to anyone in the Penn Community! Come join us for an adventure anytime! We meet weekly to debrief past trips, plan future trips, do silly activities, and often eat snacks :) We also offer opportunities to learn outdoor skills throughout the year, and have events on and off campus to get people connected and touching grass!

description: We are a student dance troupe at the University of Pennsylvania seeking to celebrate and educate the community on Pan-Asian culture through traditional, modern, and fusion dances, and to establish an organization in which people of all nationalities can learn to express themselves through the art of dance!

name: Paraguayans at Penn
description: Mba'éichapa! We're a community of undergraduate and graduate Paraguayan students at Penn. We meet regularly to cure the techaga'u while enjoying some good food and conversations. Send us an email if you want to join us!

description: Pediatric Childhood Cancer Coalition @Penn (PCCC) is a student organization at the University of Pennsylvania that supports the childhood cancer community through service initiatives and advocacy. We represent a volunteer base of students dedicated to bettering the lives of children with cancer.

name: Pen to Paper
description: Pen to Paper is a student organization dedicated to creative writing. Through workshops, critique circles, mentorship, and other activities, we hope to cultivate and uplift the creative voices of students coming from marginalized backgrounds. Often, people with these identities feel pressured to speak solely about one experience or not speak at all. We want Pen to Paper to be an avenue through which everyone can write freely. name: Penn Association for Gender Equity (PAGE)
description: The Penn Association for Gender Equity (PAGE) promotes gender and social justice and serves as an umbrella organization for a diverse range of constituent groups at Penn that serve people of martinalized genders.

name: Penn Band
description: The Penn Band was founded in 1897, making us one of the oldest student groups on campus. With about 150 members from 25 states and 14 countries, we are also one of the biggest groups at Penn and one of the largest bands in the Ivy League. We assemble over 100 times each academic year, making us among the most active college bands in the country.

name: Penn Carey Law DC Club
description: The Penn Carey Law DC Club unites members of the Penn Law community who are interested in Washington, DC. We will have formal and informal events to learn about the unique legal landscape in the DC area and to build a network among peers and alumni in the region. The group is inclusive, creating spaces to bring students together who are interested in life inside the Beltway and navigating the myriad career opportunities available to lawyers in DC.

name: Penn Carey Law Real Estate Club
description: The Penn Carey Law Real Estate Club works in conjunction with Wharton’s Zell & Laurie Real Estate center to provide an opportunity for law students interested in the real estate industry to participate in meetings, panel discussions and informal activities with students, academics and business professionals who share a passion for real estate. Law students in the Penn Carey Law Real Estate club are given the chance to meet with some of the biggest names in the industry and develop a one-on-one rapport with active professionals though the Zell & Laurie mentorship program.

name: Penn Carey Law Softball Club
description: The Penn Carey Law Softball Club aims to provide a fun and competitive environment for law students outside the classroom. We occasionally compete in recreational leagues in the fall and spring, or meet for intermittent practices throughout the year. The club's main event is the annual UVA Law School Softball Tournament in April. The club fields multiple competitive and casual teams for this weekend event.

name: Penn Carey Law Tennis Club
description: We make tennis accessible and fun for everyone by providing an encouraging community to play, watch, or simply discuss tennis on campus. Whether you have never played tennis before and want a place to learn, played in college and want some match play, or just want to come with us to watch tennis, we would love to have you in our community!

name: Penn Carey Law Veterans Club
description: The mission of Penn Carey Law Veterans is to promote military veteran recruiting, retention of military veteran admitted students, and advancement of veteran interests at Penn Carey Law. The group will also provide opportunities for veteran fellowship and advancement, organize veteran recruitment events, and provide a single voice to the staff and faculty for veteran specific issues.

name: Penn Club Squash
description: The Penn Club Squash Team is a co-ed, all-levels team for anyone interested in the sport of squash! We have 3 optional practices per week and >15 matches per semester. Although our primary focus is on road cycling, we have a sizable triathlon contingent. We even host winter cross-training to help members stay at their best when the weather gets low. Our mission is to promote progressive political values on and off campus through dialogue and action. description: Penn Dhamaka is the University of Pennsylvania’s premier competitive all-male fusion dance troupe, dedicated to celebrating the diversity of South Asian dance and culture through high-energy performances that blend Bhangra, Hip-Hop, Bollywood, Kuthu, Raas, and other dance styles. Our mission is to share our passion for dance, entertainment, and cultural expression with communities across the country while fostering brotherhood, teamwork, and a strong sense of community among our members.

name: Penn Equestrian Team
description: The Penn Equestrian Team is a student group at the University of Pennsylvania comprised of riders who compete in the IHSA or ride recreationally. Riders come from all different backgrounds and varying level of experiences. All Penn students are welcome to join the team!

name: Penn for LiNK (Liberty in North Korea)
description: Penn for Liberty in North Korea is a student organization dedicated to standing with the North Korean people as they face one of the biggest challenges confronting humanity today. We exist to empower the North Korean people as they drive progress inside their country. As an organization, we focus on fundraising, creating discussion, and raising awareness for human rights issues regarding the North Korean people.

name: Penn for Refugee Empowerment
description: Penn for Refugee Empowerment (PRE) is a student organization at the University of Pennsylvania. PRE's mission is to empower refugees through education assistance and to foster a welcoming community for refugees to build their own success in Philadelphia. PRE members engage directly with refugees and support their educational pursuits through tutoring. description: Penn Heroes is a student group at the University of Pennsylvania. The commitment level for Penn Heroes is totally up to you! You can represent us as a hospital volunteer, lead in a fundraiser, or create videos/cards to cheer up a patient in need. Whether you want to raise money, race for people's health, visit hospitals and patients weekly, or just make fun content, we would love to have you with us!

name: Penn History Review
description: Founded in 1991, the Penn History Review is a journal for undergraduate historical research. Published twice a year through the Department of History, the journal is a non-profit publication produced by and primarily for undergraduates. The editorial board of the Review is dedicated to publishing the most original and scholarly research submitted for our consideration. For more information about submissions, or about becoming an Editor, please contact us at phrsubmissions@gmail.com. Past issues of the PHR can be found at repository.upenn.edu/phr.

We've worked across impact areas including healthcare, education, water sanitation, conservation, and refugee rights. description: Penn Reading Initiative's mission is to utilize sociolinguistic knowledge in promoting literacy in West Philadelphia schools as part of the Netter Center.

description: We are a club team, affiliated with the University of Pennsylvania, of mainly undergraduates (grad students welcome too!) who love to ski, snowboard, and have a blast on the slopes. If you enjoy being on the mountain, you'll love being a part of our group. While there's a lot of team interaction regardless of the time of year, our season centers on five to six weekend trips typically beginning in early January and culminating in mid to late February. The Penn Symphony Orchestra rehearses and performs in historic Irvine Auditorium on Penn’s Campus.

The team performs in competitions and showcases both on and off-campus. name: PennApps
description: Founded in the fall of 2009, PennApps was the nation's first student-run college hackathon. Since then, it has spurred a revolution in the way engineering students develop and showcase their skills, spawning an entire "league" of hackathons across the nation. In past years, over a thousand students from the U.S. and other countries like Switzerland, Canada, England, and Singapore have converged in Philadelphia for the spring and fall editions of the event for a weekend of creation and discovery. name: PennSori A Cappella
description: PennSori is the premier Korean A Cappella Student Group at the University of Pennsylvania. We perform a mix of Korean and American songs of all genres (K-Pop, K-RnB, K-Ballad, K-HipHop, jazz, rock, pop, etc.) in order to serve as a cultural bridge between Korean and American cultures. We welcome students of any and all cultural backgrounds! Fluency in Korean is not at all required.

name: Pennsylvania Players
description: For over 85 years, the Pennsylvania Players have been bringing theater to the University of Pennsylvania. Since 1936, Penn Players has offered a creative outlet to a wide variety of students, including actors, singers, dancers, musicians, designers (scenic, lighting, costumes, properties), producers, stage managers, and others. With the guidance of professional directors (and musical directors for our musicals), Penn Players produces two major shows each year, a musical in the fall and a drama in the spring. name: Pennsylvania Six-5000 (Penn Six)
description: Penn Six is Penn's premiere parody comedy acapella group. Just a bunch of people who like to sing, and long walks on the beach... We perform A cappella arrangements from all different genres! Sketch comedy included at no additional charge. We are also a NO AUDITION group, and accept members of all experience levels! [a student group of the University of Pennsylvania, MDCCXL]

name: Penntorship (Dental)
description: Serving West Philadelphia's youth through academic enrichment, career exploration, and oral health education.

name: Penny Loafers A Cappella
description: Founded in 1986, the Penny Loafers, or Loaf, is the University of Pennsylvania’s only all-gender indie-pop a cappella group. They perform an eclectic mix of songs from your favorite artists and ones you might not have have heard of before -- they love introducing people to new music! They're also a competition group -- they compete in the International Championship of A Cappella (ICCA) annually. In their first year competing in 2024, they won their quarterfinal and moved onto semifinals.

name: PennYo A Cappella
description: PennYo is Penn's premier Chinese student a cappella group and the first collegiate Chinese a cappella group in the United States. We hope to spread the love for Chinese music to the Philadelphia community and beyond. We welcome students of all backgrounds to audition! Chinese proficiency is not required (we have members from all around the world)! All of our arrangements are written by current and past PennYo members. Check out our instagram

name: People for Immigrant Rights
description: People for Immigrant Rights is the first organization at the University of Pennsylvania led by undocumented youth and allies looking to increase the dialogue on immigration. We look to provide a safe space to discuss the issues pertinent to the current immigration system and their effect on the community. Through such discussions we hope to engage the Penn community on behalf of equal access to higher education and equal opportunities for immigrant students regardless of immigration status. Our priority is to empower undocumented students and immigrant communities to raise their voices and cha

name: Persian Students Association at Penn
description: Penn Persian Society is a student group at the University of Pennsylvania that seeks to promote Persian social and cultural awareness on Penn's campus. We also serve as a support group for Persians at Penn. It is a great way to get involved in Iranian culture and meet others who have appreciation for it! We have regular social events, celebrate cultural holidays, have opportunities to practice our Farsi together, and plan an annual Persian New Year Nowruz festival in March that is open to the general public of Philadelphia.

name: Peruvian Student Association
description: The Peruvian Student Association at the University of Pennsylvania, also known as Peru@Penn, seeks to promote, represent and celebrate Peruvian culture both on and off campus, creating an inclusive space that unites students from Peru, the Peruvian diaspora, and anyone interested in our history and traditions. Our mission is to foster cultural pride, learning and exchange through social and artistic activities that strengthen the bonds between the Peruvian students and the Penn environment. We also aim to serve as a bridge between students, alumni and the Peruvian community in Philadelphia.

name: Phi Delta Epsilon
description: What is Phi Delta Epsilon? Phi Delta Epsilon International Medical Fraternity creates physicians of integrity with a lifelong commitment to our guiding principles of philanthropy, deity, and education through fellowship, service, mentoring, and leadership. We have a chapter of around 80 members with diverse backgrounds and interests. What We Do In our chapter, we strive to foster a community of pre-med students through a variety of social, service, philanthropy, and educational events. We pride ourselves for our balance between social and professional development programming. We are a tight-kn

name: Phi Gamma Nu (PGN) Professional Business Fraternity
description: Phi Gamma Nu is a student group at the University of Pennsylvania that proudly upholds Three National Pillars which represent the underlying ideals of the fraternity. Through Professionalism, Phi Gamma Nu seeks to constantly spread interest in the business field throughout college campuses. To this end, the National Board promotes the chapters' organization of creative professional events. Through Philanthropy, Phi Gamma Nu chapters are able to build strong bonds with their respective communities as well. As the fraternity's brothers believe in civic responsibility, chapters nationwide organiz

name: Philadelphia Oral Cancer Walk/5K
description: The Philadelphia Oral Cancer Walk & 5K has been an annual tradition at Penn Dental Medicine since 2009 created and organized entirely by students. Our mission is to raise awareness about oral cancer and raise money for the PDM Oral Cancer fund, which supports oral cancer research.

name: Philippine Association (PPA)
description: We are a student group at the University of Pennsylvania with a goal to promote the awareness and appreciation of Philippine culture through cultural dance performances, potlucks, cooking sessions, karaoke, discussion forums, and most importantly, spending quality time with each other. Our club is open to anyone, regardless of ethnicity or background!

name: Philly Music Mentoring Program
description: PMMP is a group of undergraduate students at the University of Pennsylvania dedicated to enriching the lives of local K-12 students through weekly music education and mentorship. We partner with several community organizations and local schools to offer free private music lessons (in piano, percussion, strings, brass, and more), field trips, and performance opportunities to students in the wider West Philadelphia area. We are always in need of dynamic and inspiring music mentors. No previous music teaching experience is required – all we ask is that you are patient, dedicated, and compassionat

name: Philomathean Society
description: The Philomathean Society is a student club at the University of Pennsylvania that exists for those who feel that college should be about more than getting a degree. Our mission is to increase the learning of the members and the academic prestige of the University. Philo is what its members make of it. Philo gives its members the resources to bring in speakers from all over the country (and sometimes internationally!), host small teas with Penn professors, and give talks on topics they find interesting. We also boast our own club space on the fourth floor of College Hall with our own library, m

name: Physical Exam Access for Community High Schools (PEACH) at Penn
description: PEACH is a student-led organization at the University of Pennsylvania that coordinates with Penn Medicine’s physician event team to provide free and reduced-cost physical exams directly at local high schools. This work is powered by Penn undergraduate and medical student volunteers working alongside physicians, at no cost to families. Beyond physicals, PEACH is committed to inspiring and empowering student-athletes. Planned initiatives include partnering with the Netter Center and Penn Athletics to bring students to Penn sporting events, hosting nutrition workshops with hands-on demonstrations

name: Pi Lambda Sigma
description: Pi Lambda Sigma (POLIS) is the University of Pennsylvania's premier professional government society. A nonpartisan club d esigned for students interested in pursuing a career in government, POLIS provides an undergraduate network of students with a passion for politics and prepares fellows for careers in their respective fields. POLIS connects students from across the University with professionals in government to enhance their ability to pursue related careers. name: Poker at Penn
description: We are the premier poker interest group at the University of Pennsylvania. We focus on teaching poker strategy and educate our members about poker, cultivating and fostering interest for the game.

name: Policy Consulting Group at Penn (PPC)
description: (All info is updated for Fall 2026). ABOUT US: The Policy Consulting Group at Penn (PPC) is a nonpartisan, pre-professional student organization presenting student-led research and policy solutions on pressing issues at all levels of government. In recent years, we’ve partnered with leading organizations — such as Freedom House, UNFPA, UNICEF and Hyundai America — on policy projects, white papers, and youth engagement strategies, sat down with UN Ambassadors and diplomats, and conducted hundreds of successful policy meetings with Senators, Congressional Representatives, and executive agencies.

name: Polish Club
description: The Polish Club connects all people of Polish heritage or interest in Polish culture at Penn and focuses specifically on uniting them with each other and the greater Polish community in Philadelphia. Traditional meals and holidays are celebrated! The Penn Polish Club is a student group at the Univesity of Pennsylvania.

name: Pre-Dental Society
description: The Pre-Dental Society provides programming and a community for undergraduate students at the University of Pennsylvania interested in dentistry and attending dental school. It provides a space for mentorship and discussion regarding being pre-dental at Penn, the Dental Admission Test (DAT), dental school application materials, and dental school in general. Throughout the year, we meet to discuss the direction of the club, organize fundraising opportunities for charitable organizations such as Operation Smile, and partake in volunteer experiences such as assisting with dental hygiene at local

name: Product Space @ Penn
description: Students in this Univeristy of Pennsylvania club will be able to find a community around product management and learning about the product lifecycle. Students will be able to learn about the different aspects of being a product manager, build their skills through consulting endeavors, and have a community to help them develop their career. Application form for Fall 2025: Coming soon

name: Programs in Religious, Interfaith, and Spiritual Matters (PRISM)
description: Programs in Religious, Interfaith, and Spiritual Matters (PRISM) cultivates meaningful interfaith relationships on campus by creating opportunities for all students of different traditions, religions, and spiritual backgrounds to connect, share experiences, and learn from one another in a safe and respectful environment.

name: QBlack
description: QBlack is a new student organization on campus that aims to create a social, informational, and comfortable safe space for Black people that identify as queer or as falling under the LGBTQ+ umbrella. This will be a consistent space for our community at Penn to connect through close social gatherings, sex education, and decompressive programming. We are open to all students.

name: Quackers Bird Club at Penn
description: We are a fun, chill group and are Penn's only birdwatching or naturalist club! We hold frequent meetings with some variation in scheduled times to help accommodate the availability of all members. Activities range from birding outings to nature-themed crafts! Absolutely no experience or prior knowledge needed - the only requirements are that you are a Penn student and have at least a smidgen of interest in birds! Hope to see you at an event soon!!

name: Quadramics Theatre Co.
description: Quadramics is a student group at Penn who form a close-knit community of people who love to create theatre and have fun together! Quadramics is also the theatre group focused on enjoying life and getting the best experience possible out of running and working on an entirely student-run production. We are fun-loving, hardworking-more-often-than-not, ridiculous, zany people who share a passion for good times and great theatre—so come join us for the fun, madness, and, as always, the drama! In the fall we produce a play, and in the spring we produce the famous Spring Fling musical. Be on the look

name: Quaker Girls Dance Team
description: We’re the Quaker Girls Dance Team, the University of Pennsylvania’s student-run spirit dance team. Founded in 2000, we perform at Penn home football and basketball halftimes, including the Philadelphia Big 5 tournament at the Wells Fargo Center. Each spring, we also participate in the NBA 76ers Halftime Show. The team is fully student-led, with all choreography, leadership, and operations managed by members. Our routines incorporate a mix of dance styles, including jazz, hip-hop, contemporary, and pom.

name: Quaker Notes
description: Quaker Notes is the University of Pennsylvania's premier, nationally acclaimed student a cappella group. We sing a wide variety of music genres: pop, rock, r&b, and alternative. Our style is entertainment and we are committed to showing our audience a good time. All of our music is arranged by current Quaker Notes and alumnae, and we arrange & learn more than 20 new songs every year! Quaker Notes is for students who are excited about sharing their passion for music and performance, ontributing to a close-knit, community, and exploring creativity through arranging, singing, and performance. name: QuakerBots
description: QuakerBots is a student group at Penn, and its first combat robotics team, where we build robots to fight in competitions across the country, such as NHRL or GSRL, as well as hosting and attending local robotics events. We don't require any experience to join, and have programs to teach the skills we use to build our robots. Join if you want to have fun with robots, learn engineering skills, and enable carnage in the ring!

name: Quakers Venture Club at Penn
description: Introduction： Penn Quakers Venture Club is student-run entrepreneurship and venture capital student organization affiliated with the University of Pennsylvania, which opens to all current students in the Penn community. Penn Quakers Venture Club focuses on knowledge-based training of venture capital and private equity, a series of investment-related seminars/workshops from alumni and mentors, campus idea pitch day, and implementing industry insight research and investment analysis report. Our Vision: Penn Quakers Venture Club serves students and alumni interested in startups and venture capita

name: Quantum Computing Club at Penn
description: Quantum Computing Club at Penn is a student organization centered on the promotion & participation of quantum information sciences across the undergraduate student body at Penn. Members interested in our efforts are welcome to get involved in: The development of quantum projects (Open-Sourced) Hackathons & other competitions Host tours of quantum science labs at Penn Conferences & networking opportunities with industry and professionals And possibly more!

name: Queer and Asian
description: Queer and Asian (Q&A) is a student group at the University of Pennsylvania dedicated to providing a safe space for the support and empowerment of LGBTQ+ and allied individuals interested in addressing issues of the queer Asian community. We host numerous social and discussion events each semester. Past events have included boba socials, chai chats, Valentine's Day mixer, ConversAsians (discussions on being Q&A), game/movie nights, picnics, and lots of other fun activities!

name: QuestBridge Scholars at Penn
description: Quest Scholars at Penn is a campus chapter of QuestBridge Scholars Network (QSN), a national community for individuals who were both selected as National College Match Finalists and attend QuestBridge college partners. This student-run group brings QuestBridge Scholars at Penn together to foster a stronger community and personal relationships, advocate for their needs, and provide all support necessary to allow QuestBridge Scholars thrive. name: Quizbowl Club at Penn
description: A student organization at the University of Pennsylvania dedicated to competing in intercollegiate quiz bowl tournaments. Our mission is to foster academic curiosity, teamwork, and a welcoming community while representing the University of Pennsylvania at the regional and national levels.

name: Raas at Penn
description: Garba Raas is an energetic Indian folk dance originating in Gujarat that has now evolved into a full-fledged competitive dance circuit in America. Formed in 2007, Raas at Penn is UPenn's very own garba/raas team composed of both undergraduate and graduate students and is an official SAC funded University of Pennsylvania club. name: Rangoli
description: Rangoli, the South Asian Association at Penn is a University of Pennsylvania student group that was formed to prolong our culture and rekindle the spirit of various Indian traditions and festivals with verve and vigor. Rangoli is proud to embark upon its twenty-fourth year as it continues to be one of Penn's completely incorporated organizations. We are open to every member of Penn's community as we try to reach out to the various other cultural groups. Rangoli is supported by the Graduate and Professional Student Assembly.

name: REACH at Penn
description: What is Reach? Reach at Penn is a student-run club dedicated to creating a community for content creators, digital marketers, and anyone interested in entertainment and social media. What do we do? 1. Community - We plan a variety of internal events that are designed to bring our members closer. description: RAP-Line is a peer helpline established by Penn students to provide peer support, information, and referrals. It's open to all students who wish to share a problem, are in need of information, or just want to talk to someone anonymously and confidentially. The service is run by trained student volunteers who have an awareness of campus resources and skills in active listening techniques. Volunteers acknowledge that they're not professional counselors, but rather peers who provide a warm, unbiased, and supportive environment conducive to self-help. description: Ready@20 is a student organization committed to bring the youth together and help them establish their walk in Christ alongside other believers. affiliated with https://www.firstlovecenter.com

name: Red Cross Club at Penn
description: Red Cross Club at Penn is a student organization at the University of Pennsylvania which acts as a link between the Philadelphia Red Cross* chapter and Penn's campus. We host volunteer opportunities like cooking dinners for Penn Transplant House patients, supporting our monthly blood drives, working to connect local families with appropriate services after disasters, and more! name: Renewal College Fellowship
description: We are the college fellowship of Renewal Presbyterian Church (4633 Cedar Avenue) on Penn's campus. We are a Christ-centered community, and we hope that through our ministry, you can have a personal encounter with Jesus Christ, learn and experience the power of the Gospel, and participate in God's great commission in this city. We invite you to join our Sunday services, large group college meetings on Fridays, and weekly community group meetings where we study God's word. name: Reproductive Justice Working Group at Penn
description: Reproductive Justice Working Group is a community-centered student group at Penn striving to protect reproductive and sexual justice by fighting for increased contraceptive & abortion access, comprehensive sex ed, repro health legislation, menstrual equity, and much more. We support repro justice work in both the Penn & Philly community by amplifying local advocacy efforts, distributing educational resources and contraceptives/menstrual products, and developing sustainable and meaningful connections with our partner orgs. name: RJ on the Street
description: RJ on the Street is a Penn graduate student-led collective formed to work towards accessible, community-based healthcare under the reproductive justice lens, as defined by SisterSong. We honor ancestral and community-based wisdom, center the experiences of Black, Indigenous, and global majority peoples, and fight for reproductive justice for ALL. Through the midwifery model of care, harm reduction strategies, sexual and reproductive health (SRH) education and advocacy, and amplification of community partners, we aim to contribute to an ecosystem of liberation, equity, and collective well-being

name: Road2Research (R2R)
description: Traditional high school summer research programs are often inaccessible to underserved students. Many established programs exacerbate the gap in educational equity by adding a price tag or rigorous requirements, but R2R bridges this gap in Philadelphia by providing early exposure to biotechnology and research through hands-on lab experiences and eye-opening mentorship. R2R is a student organization at Penn that hosts weekly lab workshops at Penn for a cohort of 20 students, with future goals to expand. name: Run Club at Penn Carey Law
description: The Penn Law Run Club builds community, resilience, and well-being by bringing students of all paces together to run, reset, and support one another throughout the school year!

name: Sargam
description: Sargam is one of America's first student groups dedicated to performing and promoting South Asian fusion music. Established in 2004 by students at the University of Pennsylvania, Sargam’s ensemble brings together a diverse set of music ranging from Hindustani, Carnatic and Western classical to South Asian and Western pop, rock, jazz, and more.

name: Science Olympiad at the University of Pennsylvania
description: Science Olympiad at the University of Pennsylvania (SOUP) is a student-run organization at the University of Pennsylvania that hosts a Science Olympiad invitational tournament and mentors local middle school and high school teams in Philadelphia to spur interest in STEM for students who might otherwise lack the opportunity. Our Purpose Science Olympiad is a non-profit organization that hosts tournaments on a regional, state, and national level with around 7,800 teams of 15 students. name: Science Policy and Diplomacy Group at Penn
description: Most students in science receive little to no training in how to communicate science to non-scientists, how to advocate for the continued role of science in policymaking, or how science can contribute to global diplomacy. To address this gap, the Science Policy and Diplomacy Group at Penn (PSPDG) creates opportunities for early-career scientists at the University of Pennsylvania to get hands-on training and experience in the fields of science communication, policy, and diplomacy. PSPDG is open to all students and staff at Penn. Sign up for our listserv on our website for up-to-date information

name: Science Research Journals at Penn
description: Science Research Journals at Penn is a student group committed to promoting and raising the visibility of undergraduate and high school research. We were the first undergraduate student-led reserach journal in the country and continue to be the premier destination for top undergraduate and high school research, receiving hundreds of submissions per year. We run two peer-reviewed journals: one showcasing high school research and another with undergraduate research. name: Service Link
description: Established in 2011 by the Center for Public Health Initiatives at Penn, Service Link is the first and leading student-led social work volunteer group at Penn. We work to connect Philadelphians with resources for good health, such as emergency and short-term housing, health insurance, subsidized food programs, financial services, and more.

name: Sikh Organization of Penn
description: Sikh Organization of Penn aims to spread awareness of the Sikh heritage and culture at the University of Pennsylvania and in the city of Philadelphia. This inclusive, student-run organization holds various social, cultural, and community service events on and off campus to promote the Sikh culture.

name: Simply Chaos
description: Simply Chaos is the University of Pennsylvania’s first and only stand-up student-run comedy collective. We perform at events around Philadelphia, sponsored campus events, and produce our own show every semester.

name: Skeptic's Dinner
description: We provide a free meal, you come and be heard during a round table discussion about thought-provoking topics and big life questions. As an undergraduate club at the University of Pennsylvania, we strive to have a dinner table that is representative of Penn's campus in terms of race, gender, socio-economic background, and religious beliefs.

name: SNUGS (Special Needs Undergraduate Swim Lessons)
description: SNUGS is a non-profit, national organization, with a student group chapter of the organization at the University of Pennsylvania. Our core mission aims to decrease the number of drownings amongst children with special needs, which is the #1 cause of death for children with intellectual disabilities. By providing free swim instruction, with your help, we believe we can make a huge difference. Many university campuses, such as UPenn, are situated near low income communities, where specialized swimming lessons are too expensive for financially-burdened parents with disabled children. name: Social Deduction Club
description: A student group at the University of Pennsylvania created primarily to let students play mafia weekly, create and administer escape rooms, movie nights, murder mystery parties and most importantly, have fun!

name: Social Entrepreneurship Movement (SEM)
description: Established in 2007, the Social Entrepreneurship Movement is a community of student consultants, entrepreneurs, and innovators dedicated to social impact. Our passion for sustainable change drives us to build new social enterprises and support existing ones through pro-bono consulting services. Social Entrepreneurship Movement is a student group at Penn.

name: Social Planning and Events Committee (SPEC)
description: ***This is a parent group to our other committees. Please search for "SPEC" within the Penn Clubs system to sign up for an individual committee*** The Social Planning and Events Committee (SPEC) is one of the branch of student governance that is responsible for planning a variety of social events and traditions on campus. There are eight committees under SPEC: Concerts, Connaissance, Film, Jazz & Grooves, Pop Up, Sound, SPEC-TRUM, and Spring Fling (Daytime). name: Society for African Internationals at Penn (SAIP)
description: We are an inclusive community of African international students at the University of Pennsylvania. Our community is dedicated to create space to showcase the beauty of our cultural identities as well as navigating different facets of life in the new environment.

name: Society for Creative Anachronism
description: The University of Pennsylvania's student-run chapter of the Society for Creative Anachronism (SCA), a non-profit volunteer educational organization. The SCA is devoted to the research and re-creation of pre-seventeenth century skills, arts, combat, culture, and employing knowledge of history to enrich the lives of participants through events, demonstrations, and other educational presentations and activities.

name: Society of Hispanic Professional Engineers (SHPE)
description: The University of Pennsylvania student-run chapter of SHPE aims to empower the Hispanic community to realize its fullest potential and to impact the world through STEM awareness, access, support, and development. Our club does a variety of events including social, c ommunity service, academic development, and professional development. Our aim is to foster an enviorment where Hispanic engineers and allies may thrive, connect, and learn from one another while advancing their own professional goals. Hope you join us! SHPE Familia

name: Society of Undergraduate Mathematicians @ Penn
description: We are a student-run organization dedicated to promoting mathematics on Penn’s campus. We organize various events throughout the year to give students a taste of not only the theoretical aspect of math but also its various applications in life. No application required to join as a general member or come to our events!

name: Society of Women Engineers (Undergraduate)
description: The Society of Women Engineers (SWE) at Penn is a collegiate chapter of the national SWE organization, a nonprofit that empowers women to achieve their full potential as engineers and leaders while promoting engineering as a force for positive change. Penn SWE advances this mission through professional development, educational outreach, community building, and advocacy for gender equity. We strive to cultivate an inclusive engineering community in which students can develop professionally, form meaningful connections, support future generations of engineers, and recognize the value of diverse

name: Sound Politicks
description: Sound Politicks is the official undergraduate journal of political science at the University of Pennsylvania. It is published annually and covers a wide range of topics related to political science. The journal accepts submissions year-round from undergraduates of any major. Board members of the journal edit the articles, run social media, and design the journal.

name: Soundworks Tap Factory
description: We are a completely student-choreographed group that performs in and produces two shows each academic year. Our unique style comes from the broad dance foundation of all our members, which includes rhythm tap, Broadway-style tap, hip-hop, jazz, and more!

name: South Asia Society
description: The South Asia Society (SAS) is a student organization dedicated to promoting cultural unity and awareness among its members and the University of Pennsylvania community. SAS's goals are: To increase awareness of and educate the Penn community about South Asian culture and heritage. To create an environment in which students are encouraged to explore and experience South Asian culture. To increase awareness among, educate, and mobilize students in order to address pertinent issues that face the entire South Asian community, the South Asian collegiate community in America, and the Penn South As

name: South Asian Women's Space
description: SAWS is a space for all people to build a warm and open community where we feel supported by each other. The group is meant to help students who identify as South Asian at the University of Pennsylvania share experiences and explore their identities, with a focus on the challenges experienced by South Asian women and other marginalized genders. We host discussions and collaborate with other groups while creating meaningful relationships.

name: Southeast Asian Circle at Penn (SEAC)
description: Southeast Asian Circle at Penn (SEAC) immerses undergraduate students in the Southeast Asian business and cultural landscape for interested students at Penn. Our organization has three main goals : Share Southeast Asian cultures and customs with students through cultural events Enrich the Southeast Asian business education of undergraduates Uplift Southeast Asian communities outside of Penn through volunteering and business consulting services

name: Sparks Dance Company
description: Sparks Dance Company (SDC) was founded in 1989 as Penn's premiere dance company dedicated to both performing and community service. The company, which is managed by undergraduate students, maintains a high technical level of many styles of dance including ballet, contemporary, jazz, tap, and hip hop. In addition to weekly technique classes, each semester culminates with a self-choreographed show. Company members also perform at other popular campus events throughout the year such as the Emily Sachs Dance Benefit, various coffeehouses, and Student Performing Arts Night. name: SPEC Concerts

name: SPEC Connaissance
description: SPEC Connaissance (Conn) is the SPEC committee tasked with bringing high-profile speakers to campus who challenge, educate, and entertain the student body. We are also committed to representing diverse perspectives. As a general body member, you will offer input into our speaker selection process and attend the event for free. This includes access to a private meet and greet with speakers. We are an open community where all ideas, viewpoints, and people are welcome! Past speakers include: 2025 - 2026: Randall Park, Penn Badgley 2024 - 2025: Haley Lu Richardson, Tyler James Williams 2023 - 2024

name: SPEC Film Society
description: SPEC Film Society is a student group at the University of Pennsylvania that hosts free film screenings and other social events. SPEC Film also has an annual speaker series, which in the past has featured famous actors, directors and producers such as Simu Liu, Spike Lee, Sean Baker, Jesse Tyler Ferguson, Joseph Gordon Levitt, Aaron Sorkin, Kenan Thompson, Michael Cera, Woody Harrelson, and others. Past Events: Film Trivia Night Various socials Movie screenings

name: SPEC Jazz & Grooves
description: Jazz & Grooves is a student group at the University of Pennsylvania that brings up-and-coming artists to Penn's campus throughout the year. Our shows are open to Penn students. name: SPEC Pop Up
description: We plan and host a variety of free spontaneous giveaways, events, and activities throughout the year for students to enjoy a break from classes! We are a student-run committee within student government at the University of Pennsylvania.

name: SPEC Sound
description: We provide, maintain, and run the technical equipment for events hosted by a variety of student organizations, including sororities and fraternities, cultural events, bands, and more. Plus, we pay our members who work these events!

name: SPEC To Represent Undergraduate Minorities (SPEC-TRUM)
description: Welcome to the SPEC-TRUM Committee, a branch of the Social Planning and Events Committee (SPEC) and a s tudent group at the University of Pennsylvania. SPEC-TRUM (To Represent Undergraduate Minorities) events vary from free skates and movie nights to concerts, to our Tiny Desk Showcase, and in the past they have included concerts with Tierra Whack, SiR, Rico Nasty, DRAM, Aminé, and the Roots. SPEC-TRUM is open to all Penn students. For more information on everything TRUM see our powerpoint !

Our mission is to foster a community of students passionate about leveraging statistical tools to provide actionable insights for Penn Athletics. description: The mission of Stimulus Children’s Theatre Company (Stim) is to produce shows that teach valuable lessons which resonate with audiences of all ages. Students at the University of Pennsylvania share stories that communicate themes we feel are important to pass on to young audiences, such as friendship, acceptance and compassion. In addition to performing on-campus shows for our peers (typically a musical in the Fall and a play in the Spring), Stim is unique among Penn student theatre in our community service endeavours. The company was founded in 1997 and has since developed its own performance culture. This diverse company of 20+ members from all of the Penn undergraduate and graduate schools, as well as the greater Philadelphia area, seeks to explore hip-hop, jazz, contemporary, free-styling, lyrical, breaking, locking, popping, and funk, while still recognizing the personal styles of individual dancers. Funk has no limits. Each Funk show features an overarching theme, of which all numbers aim

description: The Student Harm Reduction Coalition (SHaRC) is a student-led organization at the University of Pennsylvania bringing together individuals dedicated to confronting the crisis of addiction in Philadelphia. Our members are devoted to meaningful volunteer work which provides greater opportunity for harm reduction strategies while simultaneously providing advocacy through education of our undergraduate body and Philadelphians. Our goals are two-fold. Firstly, we aim to provide clinical outreach focused on the demographic troubled with addiction through our affiliate organizations. We are currently

description: SNAP is the School of Nursing’s oldest undergraduate student organization that is committed to creating programming and opportunities for nursing students. Our programming includes studying tips , career advice from SON faculty/classmates , tips on securing an externship , community service initiatives, community building events such as painting socials, wellness walks, and our annual Nursing Formal , and so much more! description: The Student Planning Association (SPA) is the University of Pennsylvania’s official Planning Student Organization (PSO) and a pre-professional student group registered with the American Planning Association (APA). SPA fosters an inclusive, interdisciplinary community for students interested in planning and urban affairs across the Weitzman School of Design and the University of Pennsylvania. Through professional development, shared resources, and open dialogue, SPA supports learning, collaboration, and critical engagement with planning practice, policy, and equity.

description: The Student-Athlete Investment Club is dedicated to empowering student-athletes with the financial knowledge, skills, and resources necessary to make informed investment decisions and build long-term wealth. By blending the discipline, teamwork, and strategic thinking honed through athletics with the principles of sound financial management, we aim to create a supportive community where student-athletes can learn, collaborate, and grow as future leaders in the world of finance. name: Student-Athletes in Medicine
description: The Student-Athletes in Medicine (SAIM) Club at the University of Pennsylvania is dedicated to supporting student-athletes pursuing careers in medicine and healthcare. Our mission is to bridge the gap between athletics and medicine by providing a strong network, educational resources, and mentorship opportunities tailored to the unique experiences of student-athletes or those who have interests in both athletics and medicine. description: Are you a Penn student interested in making a difference and having fun while doing it? Are you passionate about health and wellness? Do you like sports and fitness? Do you enjoy volunteering and working with kids? If so, this is the place to be! Students at Penn for Sports, Fitness, and Health in West Philadelphia Schools brings Penn student volunteers together to create interest and involvement in sports, fitness, and health education among students in West Philadelphia. description: We're a student group at the University of Pennsylvania. We strive to improve the educational outcomes of underprivileged students in Philadelphia. We work with students on their reading, writing, research, critical thinking, and public speaking skills. Our volunteers are passionate about promoting educational justice and creating meaningful bonds with their students. We require no experience. description: SPAid (Students Providing Aid) is a national organization dedicated to improving global health by empowering students to construct and distribute kid-friendly first aid kits to underserved communities. Vision: A healthier future by ensuring every child has access to essential first aid resources in underserved communities worldwide. Mission: To address healthcare access gaps through collaboration, education, and strategic partnerships, making a tangible impact on global health. name: Sudanese Association At Penn
description: The Sudanese Association at Penn is a student organization at the University of Pennsylvania dedicated to creating a vibrant and inclusive community that celebrates Sudanese culture and heritage. Our organization welcomes all students who are interested in learning about, engaging with, and supporting the Sudanese community and its allies.

name: Sustainability Consulting at Penn
description: OUR MISSION: Sustainability Consulting at Penn is a student-led consultancy group at the University of Pennsylvania committed to providing pro bono sustainability services to organizations across the globe, including the Americas, Australia, and Europe. Our multicultural team recommends innovative, environmentally friendly, and cost-effective solutions that prioritize the needs of all stakeholders. name: Table Tennis at Penn
description: Table Tennis at Penn is a student group at the University of Pennsylvania that holds open practices. No tryouts or time commitments are required to join the club, so drop by any practice to say hi and play some ping pong! If you're interested in competition, we have a recreational team that plays friendly scrimmages and a competitive team that travels to play schools around the country. Whether you are a beginner, an accomplished tournament player, or just someone looking to have fun - we have a place for you in our club!

name: Tabletop at Penn
description: Tabletop at Penn brings students together through tabletop role-playing games (TTRPGs), including Dungeons & Dragons, homebrew campaigns, and Adventurers League adventures. We also foster a creative community for aspiring and experienced RPG developers, artists, and writers to develop, share, and playtest original science fiction and fantasy worlds, stories, and game content.

It is currently led by several of his students, black belts and master black belts, who continue to offer Penn students, Tae Kwon Do in a traditional setting which emphasizes both mental and physical conditioning. description: We welcome students (graduates included) of all levels! Follow us on Instagram @penntaekwondo to stay updated.

description: Taiwanese Society at Penn is a network and community for Penn students who are interested in Taiwanese culture and affairs. We foster culture and community for both members and the greater Penn community through family group dinners, boba socials, educational workshops, dim sum trips, karaoke nights, and semester-end keystone events: Next Stop Taiwan and Night Market. name: Taiwanese Student Association @ Penn
description: The Taiwanese Student Association (TSA) is a graduate student group at the University of Pennsylvania (Penn) dedicated to fostering community, cultural connection, and engagement around Taiwanese affairs among graduate and professional students and the broader Penn community. Through cultural, social, educational, and professional programming, TSA seeks to strengthen connections across Penn and promote an inclusive, connected campus community.

name: TEDxPenn

We hold a license at the University of Pennsylvania to host the largest student-run TEDx conference in the world, and today our TED Talks have amassed over 15 million views on YouTube with a wide range of speakers, from OpenAI executives to Penn professors to the creator of Apple Emojis. This coming spring, we plan to host our annual conference, where 1000+ attendees are invited to engage with TED Talks related to technology, entertainment, and design.

name: Thai Students Association at Penn
description: Thai Student Association at the University of Pennsylvania, also more affectionately and unofficially known as PennThai was founded in 1995. The association now comprise more than 40 undergraduate and graduate students, both Thai and non-Thai, who are interested to learn more about our heritage. Over the years, we have become a more active student group on campus, organizing a plethora of events for our members and the Penn community, ranging from small gatherings to our signature extravaganza, Thai Night! name: The Accountability Initiative
description: The Accountability Initiative-Penn chapter is a student led organization of young advocates at the University of Pennsylvania dedicated to connecting the UPenn and West Philadelphia Community through advocacy, mentorship, and service. We offer Higher Education workshops to West Philadelphia High Schools on topics ranging from College Readiness and Financial Literacy to Trade School and Resume Building.

name: The AgriBusiness Club
description: The Agribusiness Club is a student group at the University of Pennsylvania. We pride ourselves in being a tight-knit community of Penn students interested in everything ag. From cocoa research in Ghana to advising NASA Space Crops to consulting for leading biotech firms, our members gain hands-on, real-world experiences across the industry. Wharton's Rising Club of the Year Wharton's Best Emerging Club Ivy League's First AgriBusiness Club

name: The Alt Protein Project at Penn
description: The Alt Protein Project at Penn is a chapter of the Good Food Institute (GFI) Alt Protein Project, a global student movement dedicated to turning universities into engines for alternative protein education, research, and innovation. The program enables motivated, visionary students to lead their universities to transform the way we produce food - creating a food system that is sustainable, secure, and just. description: Andean Representation is an organization designed for the spread, advancement, and acknowledgment of Andean culture at the University of Pennsylvania. Our focus is to facilitate cultural, academic, and social events relevant to the countries of the Andes region, including, but not limited to, Ecuador, Peru, Bolivia, Venezuela, Colombia, Argentina and Chile. name: The Appétit
description: The Appétit is the University of Pennsylvania's innovative, student-run magazine covering all things food . Throughout the year, we publish eye-catching magazines, host events with high-profile restaurateurs, and trek through Philly and beyond for the greatest food finds. Find a place in our organization by becoming a writer, photographer, designer, or recipe developer! If you want more hands-on experiences, you can help us plan a new host of events, establish relations within the food industry, run our food blog, or volunteer directly in the Philly community, to name a few.

name: The Black Scientist Collective
description: Black Scientist Collective (BSC) is a student organization at the University of Pennsylvania dedicated to fostering community and opportunities for Black students across pre-health and STEM disciplines within the university and the wider Philadelphia area. Our mission is to unite Black scientific minds on campus while empowering members to excel academically, professionally, and clinically. description: The Christian Association (CA) is a student community of hospitality, service & advocacy, and faith exploration. Our weekly gathering for dinner and discussion is on Wednesday evenings. We also have at least monthly opportunities for service and social activities. description: The Disabled Coalition seeks to create a safe space for the University of Pennsylvania’s disabled community to build authentic connections and support one another. The space is designed by and for the disability community to serve as a platform to collaborate among students, faculty, and staff. We aim to empower the disabled community on campus through education. We support students with all types of disabilities, including mental and physical disabilities. description: The Epistle at Penn is a Christian journal dedicated to sharing and echoing the words of Christ's followers. We encourage and accept all students from diverse backgrounds to share their testimonies, emotions, beliefs, and experiences about their religious journeys. This organization hopes to become a vessel for the Lord's words in order to comfort, support, and inspire believers and nonbelievers to pursue and deepen their faith. name: The Excelano Project
description: The Excelano Project is the University of Pennsylvania’s first and premier spoken word group. Supposedly derived from Latin, “excelano” means “we march forth” and from its foundation in 2001 by poets and then Penn students Carlos Gomez and Warren Longmire, EP has been doing just that. In 2007 and 2009, we had the pleasure of taking home the College Union’s Poetry Slam Invitational title. Our mission is to live practically as Christians and reflect the glory of God as His image-bearers. description: T he Italian Club @ Penn is the premier community for Penn students interested in all things Italian. We welcome students with a diverse range of cultural experiences and language ability, with a deep interest in Italian culture. No proficiency in the Italian language is required! But we will help you achieve confidence in your Italian skills. We collaborate with the Italian Department and host a number of events both in and off campus.

name: The Jazz Ensemble at Penn
description: The Jazz Ensemble at Penn (formerly known as Penn Jazz ) is the big band jazz ensemble at the University of Pennsylvania . The group is student-run and led, with the assistance of musical director Dr. Ryan Tomski. Undergraduate and graduate students are all welcome. The Jazz Ensemble at Penn was formed in the fall of 1973 and has performed with numerous jazz legends throughout its history, such as Dizzy Gillespie, McCoy Tyner, the Count Basie Orchestra, Wynton Marsalis, and most recently, Christian McBride. name: The Moviegoer
description: The Moviegoer is a student-run organization at the University of Pennsylvania dedicated to film and media criticism. Our mission is to provide insightful coverage of popular culture, written by and for the Penn community. We publish articles on our website and on social media, organize screening events for our members, and hold weekly meetings in the Kelly Writer’s House–open to all. The Moviegoer seeks to provide a safe and inviting space for writers and movie buffs to come together and share their opinions.

description: Devoted to the literary and visual arts, we are a student group and a professional literary magazine that publishes original poetry, fiction, creative nonfiction, and visual artwork, and feature a blend of emerging and established voices in our biannual print and online publication. In our seven-decade history, we’ve published works by William Carlos Williams, Allen Ginsberg, e. e. cummings, and Jennifer Egan, among others. name: The Pennchants
description: The Pennchants are the University of Pennsylvania's premier all-male a cappella group. A highly professional student-run group that balances touring, recording, and high-profile performances, the Pennchants have earned widespread recognition as a group that delivers fresh energy and never fails to win over audiences' hearts with their distinct blend of pop, rock, and the songs of our childhood. Under the guidance of the Petey Greene Program, we provide one-on-one or small group tutoring in order to supplement educational programming in neighboring correctional institutions.

name: The Shea Collective
description: The Shea Collective is a student group created in order to connect Black people at The University of Pennsylvania who experience misogynoir (prejudice those who are perceived or socialized as black women) and to strengthen our community. We plan to offer a space of mentorship, a support system, resources, forums/discussions, socials, and bonding events in order to connect with each other in our community. Our club is open to all who are interested.

name: The Social Impact Consulting Group [SIC]
description: Wharton’s Social Impact Consulting (SIC) group is a student-organized group that provides pro-bono consulting services to local, national, and even international organizations with social missions. New member applications are accepted at the beginning of each semester. The Social Impact Consulting Group exposes University of Pennsylvania students to the field of non-profit and social enterprise consulting and encourages students to develop an understanding of social responsibility as they proceed in their personal and professional careers. Come meet us at one of our Spring 2026 info sessions!

name: The Songwriters Collective
description: Songwriters Collective is Penn's premiere group for student songwriters. Working collaboratively, with an intention of building intimate and safe community, we create sets of entirely new music and perform together each semester. We meet weekly on Sundays to jam together, workshop our songs and collaborate on new music through writing exercises and prompts.

name: The Student Committee on Undergraduate Education (SCUE)
description: SCUE seeks to address any issue that affects undergraduate education and the intellectual atmosphere at Penn. We work to enhance and expand curricular opportunities, advising, academic options, and the overall quality of the undergraduate academic experience. We serve our duty as advocates for the student body and as advisors to the faculty and administration.

name: The Undergraduate Law Journal at Penn
description: A student-run research publication, the Undergraduate Law Journal at Penn (formerly known as PULJ) seeks to foster scholarly discourse on topical and historical issues pertaining to law or the legal system. In this spirit, the journal's principal objective is to publish exceptional undergraduate works, drawn from an array of disciplinary perspectives, that evaluate and elucidate the intricacies, vagaries, and nuances of law as they relate to domestic and international affairs, business, academia, and society. name: The University of Pennsylvania Glee Club
description: The University of Pennsylvania Glee Club is an extracurricular performing organization with four sections: a choir, pit band, technical crew, and accompanist section. The Glee Club performs three major concerts each year. The group sings at official campus events, as well as gigs around Philadelphia and other states in the area. Each spring, the group tours internationally. The Club blends heritage with modern artistry, preserving Penn’s traditions while showcasing choral and theatrical art forms. The Club is dedicated to musical excellence and fellowship.

name: The WALK Magazine
description: Launched in 2006, The WALK Magazine is the University of Pennsylvania’s premier and completely student-run fashion publication and community. In 2010, thewalkmag.com was launched as a sister to the print edition, providing Penn with its widely-demanded fashion fix year round. As an organization, The WALK strives to explore the interdisciplinary field of fashion through its diverse and talented staff members.

name: Theta Tau
description: Theta Tau is a student organization at the University of Pennsylvania. As Penn's premier professional engineering fraternity, our purpose is to develop and maintain a high standard of professional interest among its members, and to unite them in a strong bond of fraternal fellowship. Our three pillars of professional development, brotherhood, and service are reflected in our five-committee structure and complemented by our rush and pledge committees to keep membership fresh and enthusiastic. name: Ukrainian Student Association
description: Welcome to the Ukrainian Student Association! We aim to bring together students of Ukrainian heritage and anyone with an interest in Ukrainian culture at Penn. Our club is open to all undergraduate students, offering a space to celebrate and engage with Ukraine’s rich traditions and history. name: UMOJA
description: UMOJA speaks as the representative voice of Black students and student organizations at the University of Pennsylvania and derives its legitimacy from the consent and confidence of its membership organizations (Constituents). UMOJA is charged with uniting its Constituents into a common political voice, mobilizing its Constituents for a common agenda, and organizing its Constituents under a common calendar. While UMOJA’s mission is rooted in advancing the experiences of Black students, its programs, advocacy, and activities remain open to the entire Penn community.

name: Undergraduate Assembly (UA)
description: About the UA The Undergraduate Assembly (UA) is the elected, representative body of undergraduates at Penn, charged with improving life for all students through funding, services, and advocacy. How we work: We lobby for tangible change at Penn based on student needs We represent students to administrators and outsiders We bring students from different groups and identities together We provide services to improve student’s quality of life We fund the other branches of student government and, by extension, all student groups on campus

name: Undergraduate Chemistry Society at Penn
description: PUCS is the official ACS (American Chemical Society) Chapter at Penn established in 1940. We provide programming and professional chemistry-related events, socials, and community service in collaboration with high schools in the Philadelphia area.

name: Undergraduate Economics Society (UES)
description: The Penn Undergraduate Economics Society (Penn UES) is the largest economics organization on campus, hosting events such as speaker series, professor chats, academic discussions, and more. We provide opportunities for academic and professional growth in all areas related to economics while fostering a strong community of students from diverse majors. All are welcome!

description: The Undergraduate Geography Club is a student group at Penn that seeks to build community and world awareness through geography

name: Undergraduate Moot Court at Penn
description: We are a student group at the University of Pennsylvania that participates in the American Moot Court Association regional competitions. Moot court gives students a taste of how appellate advocacy works. Students will learn how to write 19-30 page legal briefs utilizing real case law and legal citations. Students will also be prepared to present oral arguments in front of real attorneys and sitting judges at regional competitions. name: Underrepresented Student Advisory Board in Engineering
description: USABE strives to create a welcoming, diverse and inclusive community among engineers through underrepresented student advocacy. This entails connecting, empowering, and amplifying the underrepresented voices throughout SEAS. In doing so, we aim to: Facilitate meaningful, actionable discourse around the collective experiences of our underrepresented engineers through surveys and town halls. Provide useful resources and programming centered around academic, personal, and professional development. description: UnEarthed is a student-run publication at the University of Pennsylvania that publishes creative, inspirational, and educational magazines for elementary and middle schoolers in the West Philadelphia area. Our mission is to ensure that every child has the opportunity to unearth their intellect and curiosity. Each semester, our team of writers, editors, and designers collaborates to create a magazine that we share with local children in person and online. Past articles include topics like the history of coffee, how different animals sleep, why hot water feels cold, and so much more!

name: UNICEF at Penn
description: UNICEF at Penn is a student-led organization dedicated to advancing the rights and well-being of children, in Philadelphia and around the world. Guided by UNICEF's mandate from the United Nations General Assembly, we work to ensure every child has access to health, protection, education, and opportunity. We pursue this mission through four pillars. We fundraise to support UNICEF's global programs and to sustain the campus programming, partnerships, and operations that make our work possible. Among UMC’s earliest accomplishments is staging sit-in protests that led to the establishment of the Greenfield Intercultural Center. Today, the UMC represents over 40 student groups that serve a variety of cultural communities. We provide funding for their events as well as hold our own events. By performing at hospitals, schools for children, and throughout campus, Upstage A Cappella embodies the joy of song.

We gather to notice, question, and map the dynamic ecologies between people, the built environment, and our nonhuman relatives. Upstream is a graduate student group at the University of Pennsylvania. Our work takes form through workshops, editing, experimental print and digital publications, and in-person gatherings rooted in slow collaboration. VSA is committed to being an active member of both the Penn and greater Philadelphia communities while providing a welcoming space for Vietnamese students and anyone interested in Vietnamese culture to connect, build community, and celebrate their shared interests. We welcome anyone interested in Vietnamese culture to join us!

We empower students to understand waste systems, engage with their communities, and turn ideas into action. Through education, collaboration, and hands-on initiatives, WWP works to make sustainable waste practices a meaningful part of campus life and extend their impact beyond Penn.

Our lessons are designed for elementary school students in West Philadelphia, ranging from kindergarten through sixth grade. We believe that learning essential swimming and water safety skills at a young age is crucial to helping prevent avoidable drownings and promoting lifelong water safety.
